full_judgment: Only the defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing a written statement and denying the plaintiffs title and possession in the suit lands; He contends that Arabdi's son and only ultimate heir Tomiruddin mortgaged his 8 annas interest in the lands of the disputed khatian to one Nimchand Roy who in Mortgage Execution Case No. 117/18 auction purchased Tomiruddin's interest on 6.9 18 and took khas possession thereof on 13.4.1919. Thereafter he sold the interest under a registered kabala dated 19.5.1919 in favour of Dhalai who possessed the same. After the death of Dhalai his heirs and successive heirs including the defendants possessed the same. Ainuddin, a deceased grandson of Arabdi took settlement of .42 acres of land of the disputed holding for 12 years on payment of Tk. 50 as salami and at an annual rental of 9/- executing a registered kol karsha kabuliyat on 18.9.29 in favour of Montaruddin, son of Dhalai. The Kabuliyat was executed by Ainuddin on his own behalf and on behalf of plaintiff Nos. 1 & 2, then minors. This under-tenancy fell into arrears of rent and in Rent Execution Case No. 273/44 Montazuddin auction purchased the land and took delivery of possession thereof on 19.6.44 by evicting the plaintiffs and since then the defendants are in possession of the lands of the entire holding.
